target: ट्रैफ़िक कम होगा तो हम टाइम पर पहुँच जाएँगे।
english: If there's less traffic, we'll get there on time.
reason: Proverb/motto ("if the foundation is strong the building will stand") — a copybook aphorism, not speech. Replacement keeps the same X होगा तो Y होगा future-conditional in an everyday situation.

target: हमारे घर में रोज़ सुबह अख़बार पढ़ा जाता है।
english: In our house the newspaper is read every morning.
reason: Preachy values statement ("we respect elders"), and the subjectless हमारे परिवार में ... करते हैं is grammatically off. Replacement keeps the हमारे घर में + habitual passive frame with ordinary content.

target: अमृतसर में स्वर्ण मंदिर देखने बहुत लोग आते हैं।
english: A lot of people come to see the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
reason: Guidebook copy ("an example of magnificent architecture") — nobody talks like this. Replacement keeps the same place name and a simple है-statement in spoken register.

target: काम जल्दी ख़त्म होगा तो हम फ़िल्म देखने चलेंगे।
english: If the work finishes early, we'll go watch a movie.
reason: Generic third-person primer line about crops and farmers — nothing a learner will ever say. Same X होगा तो Y future-conditional, everyday content.

target: मेहमानों को पहले खाना परोसा जाता है।
reason: Vacuous family-values filler ("the son-in-law is respected"). Replacement keeps the को + habitual passive (जाता है) pattern with something actually usable at home.

target: संदूक में पुराने कपड़े और बचपन की चीज़ें रखी हैं।
english: Old clothes and childhood things are kept in the trunk.
reason: "याद की चीज़ें" is not idiomatic Hindi (translationese for "memorabilia"). Same locative + रखी हैं sentence with a phrase people actually use.

target: देर तक घुटने मोड़कर बैठने से पैर दुखने लगते हैं।
english: Sitting with your knees bent for a long time makes your legs hurt.
reason: Culture-note trivia ("sitting with knees bent is common in India") — reads like a guidebook footnote. Replacement keeps घुटने मोड़कर + the -कर converb in a sentence a person would say.

target: चुकंदर का रस मेरी माँ रोज़ सुबह पीती हैं।
english: My mother drinks beetroot juice every morning.
reason: Folk-health claim ("beetroot juice boosts blood") — pointless trivia for a learner. Same vocabulary, same habitual present, now a real thing someone says.

target: बक्से के ताले में ज़ंग लग गया, अब खुल नहीं रहा।
english: The box's lock has rusted, now it won't open.
reason: "ताला ज़ंग से जाम हो गया" is translationese; Hindi says ताले में ज़ंग लग गया. Also swaps the odd English loan बॉक्स for बक्सा. Same हो गया / लग गया perfective.

target: सारे बर्तन धोकर अलमारी में रख दिए गए।
english: All the utensils were washed and put in the cupboard.
reason: Pure officialese with no content ("all documents were verified") — a form-processing line, not speech. Same passive perfective (किए गए → रख दिए गए) in a household context.

target: कमरे के कोने में एक पुरानी मूर्ति रखी है।
english: An old statue is placed in the corner of the room.
reason: Museum-catalogue register (मुख्य कक्ष, प्रतिमा) that a learner will never produce. Same के ... में + रखी है locative with everyday words (कोना, मूर्ति).

target: निखिल ने ज़ोर देकर कहा कि वो कल ज़रूर आएगा।
english: Nikhil insisted that he will definitely come tomorrow.
reason: The कि-clause drops its subject ("कि सच बोल रहा है"), which is ungrammatical here, and it duplicates hi-2587. Same ज़ोर देकर कहा कि reported-speech pattern with a complete clause and different content.

target: छोटे लड़के ने भारी बैग खुद उठा लिया।
english: The little boy picked up the heavy bag himself.
reason: "ठिगना" is a rare, faintly insulting word no beginner needs, and the sentence is an adjective drill. Same adjective + ने-perfective structure with common vocabulary.

target: मैंने पेचकस से खिड़की का पेंच कस दिया।
english: I tightened the window screw with a screwdriver.
reason: "बल्ब का धारक" is wrong Hindi (धारक = a bearer/holder of a document, not a fitting) and the subject is missing. Same instrumental से + perfective, with a natural object.

target: टिकट बुक कर दी गई और सामान भी बँध गया।
english: The ticket was booked and the luggage got packed too.
reason: Contentless bureaucratic boilerplate ("complaint filed, action started") — the deck already has a concrete complaint sentence at hi-2194. Same two-clause passive perfective in everyday register.

target: गर्मियों में सत्तू का शरबत बहुत अच्छा लगता है।
english: Sattu sharbat tastes really good in the summer.
reason: Textbook health claim ("gives strength") and सत्तू का घोल is the wrong collocation — people say सत्तू का शरबत. Same seasonal habitual-present frame.

target: दाँत का इलाज समय पर करवा लो।
english: Get your tooth treated on time.
reason: Preachy public-health advice on a niche ailment (piles) a learner will not discuss. Same इलाज ... करवाओ causative imperative with a complaint people actually mention.

target: हम पेड़ के नीचे बैठकर चाय पीते हैं और बातें करते हैं।
english: We sit under the tree drinking tea and chatting.
reason: Idyllic school-essay line ("we study peacefully under shady trees") — says nothing usable. Same के नीचे बैठकर + habitual present in an ordinary scene.
